intro: When a nor'easter dumps eight inches on the Main Line overnight, the difference between a normal morning and a missed workday is whether someone showed up to clear your driveway. That's the entire job we've built this service around: you sign up once, and every time it snows, our crew shows up automatically — no phone call, no waiting on a guy with a plow who may or may not answer.

We focus on the residential driveways of Lower Merion Township and the Main Line — the long, tree-lined driveways of Gladwyne and Penn Valley, the sloped approaches of Bryn Mawr and Villanova, and the paver, cobblestone, and gravel drives of Ardmore, Wynnewood, and Bala Cynwyd that most plow operators either skip or scar. Every visit includes your driveway plowed or snow-blown, walkways and steps hand-cleared with shovels (never scraped by a machine), and optional salt or ice-melt so nothing refreezes overnight.

JD Home Construction is a licensed Pennsylvania contractor (PA #214497), fully insured. We build, pour, and repair driveways in the off-season — which means we clear yours with equipment and technique that protect the surface, whether it's concrete, asphalt, pavers, cobblestone, or gravel.

faqs.q: How much does residential snow removal cost in Lower Merion?
faqs.a: Pricing is a flat rate per visit based on driveway size and length, walkway footage, slope, and whether salting is included — a long Gladwyne driveway prices differently than a two-car drive in Ardmore. Seasonal contracts bundle unlimited storms into one price and work out cheaper in a normal winter (roughly 4–8 plowable events). Send us your address through the form and we'll return an exact flat-rate quote within 24 hours — no obligation, and for most homes no site visit is needed.

faqs.q: Do you handle long or steep Main Line driveways?
faqs.a: Yes — they're our specialty. Long, tree-lined drives in Gladwyne and Penn Valley, sloped approaches in Bryn Mawr and Villanova, and shared private lanes are exactly what our truck-mounted plow and crew are set up for. If your current plow operator skips your driveway when the storm gets heavy, that's precisely the client we built our priority routes for.

faqs.q: When do you come after it snows?
faqs.a: Crews dispatch automatically once accumulation reaches your trigger depth (2 inches standard). For longer storms we clear once during the storm and return after it ends. Every property is cleared within 12 hours of snowfall ending — seasonal contract clients are routed first and are typically cleared before the morning commute.

faqs.q: Do I have to call you each time it snows?
faqs.a: No — that's the point. We monitor every storm all winter. If your plan's trigger depth is met, your address is automatically on a route. You'll get a photo confirmation text when your driveway, walkways, and sidewalk are clear.

faqs.q: What are the sidewalk snow removal laws in Lower Merion and Philadelphia?
faqs.a: Lower Merion Township code requires a pathway at least 36 inches wide cleared on your sidewalk within 24 hours after snow or sleet stops falling — and if ice is frozen too hard to remove safely, the sidewalk must be treated with salt or abrasives. Philadelphia is stricter: a 36-inch path within just 6 hours. Both issue fines for violations. Sidewalk clearing is included in all of our residential plans, so you stay compliant automatically.

faqs.q: Will plowing damage my paver, stamped concrete, or gravel driveway?
faqs.a: Not the way we do it. We install and pour driveways in the off-season, so we match the method to the surface: rubber-edged blades and adjusted skid shoes on pavers and stamped concrete, snow-blowers or raised blades over gravel, and hand tools around edges, aprons, and drains. Tell us your surface in the quote form and we assign the right equipment.

faqs.q: Do you apply salt, and is it safe for pets and concrete?
faqs.a: Yes — salting is included in seasonal contracts and available as an add-on for per-storm service. We use standard rock salt on asphalt and offer calcium/magnesium-based, pet-safer ice melt for concrete, pavers, and homes with dogs. Just tell us your preference when you sign up.

faqs.q: Do you clear the pile the city plow leaves at the end of my driveway?
faqs.a: Yes. The end-of-driveway berm — the heavy, compacted ridge municipal plows push back across your apron — is included in every visit. If the city plow comes through after we've cleared, seasonal clients can request a berm-only return visit.

faqs.q: Are you licensed and insured?
faqs.a: Yes. JD Home Construction operates under Pennsylvania Contractor #214497 and carries full general liability insurance. You're hiring an established Philadelphia construction company, not an unmarked truck — and that matters the day something goes wrong on your property.

faqs.q: Can I set this up for an elderly parent's house?
faqs.a: Absolutely — a large share of our seasonal clients are set up by adult children for a parent's home. We handle billing with you, clear their property automatically every storm, and send you the photo confirmation so you know it's done without having to check in.

ctaText: Every year we cap each route so we can honor the 12-hour guarantee. Lock in your driveway now — get a flat-rate quote in 24 hours.

intro: Half of Philadelphia's housing stock has plaster-and-lath walls, and the other half has drywall installed over framing that's seen a century of settling. Interior work here isn't just hanging board — it's knowing when to skim-coat original plaster, when to replace it, how to frame level walls in an out-of-level rowhouse, and how to match 100-year-old trim profiles so a repair disappears.

We provide precise framing, seamless drywall installation and finishing, professional painting, and custom millwork — trim, crown molding, wainscoting, and built-ins that add the architectural detail Philadelphia homes deserve.

whyUs.title: Old-house fluent
whyUs.text: Plaster walls, true-dimension lumber, and settled floors don't surprise us — they're the standard Philadelphia condition we build around.

whyUs.title: Millwork that matches
whyUs.text: We replicate historic trim profiles and build custom pieces, so new work blends seamlessly with a home's original character.

whyUs.title: Clean, protected job sites
whyUs.text: Dust containment, floor protection, and daily clean-up — because you're living in the house while we work.

faqs.q: Should I repair my plaster walls or replace them with drywall?
faqs.a: It depends on condition. Plaster in decent shape is often worth saving with a skim coat — it's denser and quieter than drywall. Plaster that's delaminating from the lath, badly cracked, or hiding wiring work that needs to happen is usually better replaced. We assess wall by wall and give you an honest recommendation either way.

faqs.q: Can you match the original trim in my old rowhouse?
faqs.a: Yes. We can replicate historic casing, baseboard, and crown profiles so repairs and additions blend with the original woodwork — critical in Society Hill, Queen Village, and other historic neighborhoods.

faqs.q: Do you do painting on its own, or only as part of bigger jobs?
faqs.a: Both. We take on standalone interior painting projects as well as paint as the finishing stage of framing, drywall, and millwork work.

faqs.q: How do you keep dust under control?
faqs.a: Plastic containment on doorways, floor protection throughout, HEPA vacuums on sanders, and daily clean-up. Drywall and plaster work is dusty by nature, but it should stay inside the work zone — not on your furniture.

We build and repair exteriors with that cycle in mind — proper housewrap and flashing behind every siding job, correct expansion control in every pour, and materials matched to how this climate actually behaves.

Our exterior services cover new-construction and replacement framing, siding in vinyl, fiber cement, wood, and metal, structural repairs, and concrete work for foundations, driveways, patios, and walkways.

faqs.q: Which siding is best for Philadelphia weather?
faqs.a: Fiber cement (like James Hardie) handles freeze-thaw, humidity, and sun exceptionally well and holds paint for years — it's our usual recommendation for owners staying long-term. Quality vinyl remains the value pick and has improved dramatically. We'll walk you through cost versus lifespan for your specific house.

faqs.q: Can you replace just a damaged section of siding?
faqs.a: Often yes, especially with vinyl. The honest caveat: sun-faded existing siding rarely matches new panels perfectly. We'll tell you up front whether a repair will blend or whether the elevation is better re-sided.

faqs.q: Do you handle the concrete work too, like stoops and walkways?
faqs.a: Yes — concrete is one of our core trades. Stoop rebuilds, sidewalks, aprons, patios, and foundations are all in-house, which is why exterior packages with us don't require a second contractor.

faqs.q: Do exterior projects need permits in Philadelphia?
faqs.a: Structural work, most concrete in the public right-of-way (sidewalks), and some siding jobs require L&I permits. Historic districts add Historical Commission review for facade changes. We handle all of it as part of the project.

intro: Concrete in Philadelphia lives a hard life: freeze-thaw cycles, road salt, tree roots, and century-old sub-bases that were never compacted properly. The difference between a driveway that lasts 30 years and one that cracks in 3 is everything you can't see — excavation depth, base preparation, reinforcement, expansion control, and cure time. That's where we don't cut corners.

We pour and finish driveways, sidewalks, stoops, patios, aprons, foundations, and structural slabs for homes and businesses across Philadelphia and Bucks County — properly formed, reinforced, and finished, with L&I permits handled when the work touches the public right-of-way.

whyUs.title: Built for freeze-thaw
whyUs.text: Air-entrained mixes, correct depth, proper joints, and real cure time — the details that decide whether concrete survives Philadelphia winters.

whyUs.title: Right-of-way experts
whyUs.text: Sidewalk and curb work in Philadelphia requires city permits and spec compliance. We handle the paperwork and pour to city standard.

whyUs.title: Repair honesty
whyUs.text: If a slab can be saved, we'll say so. If it's beyond saving, we'll show you why — and quote replacement with no games.

faqs.q: How much does a concrete driveway cost in Philadelphia?
faqs.a: Driveway cost is driven by square footage, demolition of the existing surface, base condition, and finish. Replacement projects cost more than fresh pours because of removal and disposal. We measure on-site and give a firm written quote — and we're often asked to fix driveways poured cheap two years earlier, so we'll show you exactly what's in our spec.

faqs.q: How long before I can drive on new concrete?
faqs.a: Foot traffic after 24–48 hours; vehicles after 7 days; full design strength at 28 days. We'll give you exact guidance based on the mix and weather during your pour.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace my sidewalk in Philadelphia?
faqs.a: Yes — sidewalks are in the public right-of-way, and the city requires permits and specific construction standards. Homeowners are responsible for keeping their sidewalks safe and can be cited for defects. We handle the permits and pour to city spec.

faqs.q: Cracked concrete — repair or replace?
faqs.a: Hairline surface cracks can often be sealed or resurfaced. Cracks with vertical displacement, wide gaps, or multiple broken sections usually mean the base underneath has failed, and patching is throwing money away. We assess honestly and only recommend replacement when repair won't hold.

intro: A Philadelphia gut renovation is really two projects: the one you can see — kitchens, baths, floors, finishes — and the one behind the walls, where a century of knob-and-tube wiring, galvanized plumbing, and settled framing waits. We've opened up enough Philly rowhomes to quote both halves realistically, which is why our projects finish near the number they started at.

From single-room remodels to full-house transformations, we handle demolition, structural changes, all mechanical systems, and every finish trade under one contract — minimizing the time your life is disrupted and maximizing the value added to your home.

whyUs.title: We quote for what's behind the walls
whyUs.text: Knob-and-tube, cast iron stacks, and hidden framing issues are priced into our process — not discovered as change orders.

whyUs.title: Whole-house, one contract
whyUs.text: Every trade — demo through paint — managed by one team with one schedule, so the project actually moves.

whyUs.title: Value-focused decisions
whyUs.text: We'll tell you which upgrades pay back at resale and which are purely for love, so you spend intentionally.

faqs.q: How much does a gut renovation cost in Philadelphia?
faqs.a: A full gut of a typical 1,200–1,600 sq ft rowhouse — new electrical, plumbing, HVAC, kitchen, baths, and finishes — generally lands in the low-to-mid six figures depending on finish level and structural changes. We provide detailed line-item estimates after an in-home assessment so you can tune scope to budget.

faqs.q: Can I live in my house during the renovation?
faqs.a: For single-room and phased projects, usually yes. For full gut renovations, no — there's no water, power, or dust-free space for weeks at a time. We'll tell you honestly which category your project falls into before you commit.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-home renovation take?
faqs.a: Anywhere from 2 weeks for a single-space remodel to 6 months for a full gut renovation. Permits, structural work, and material lead times drive the schedule; we map it in writing before demolition starts.

faqs.q: Do you handle all the permits?
faqs.a: Yes — Philadelphia L&I permits for structural, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical work, plus township permits in the suburbs and Historical Commission coordination where applicable.
